scope: Substantive refresh of an existing post at its URL, adding sources

observations.summary: Do not pump during flooded or saturated drainfield conditions (temporary at best; tank may float out and damage inlet and outlet pipes; newer systems pop out more readily); reduce water use, the only way to prevent backup when water table is high; do not use system until drainfield water is lower than water around the house; do not drink well water until tested, contact local health department; check electrical connections; secure manhole cover and inspection ports; inspect if settling or not accepting water; most tanks not damaged but tanks and pump chambers can fill with silt; pump tank and lift station after flood; clogged absorption field may need a new system; only trained specialists clean or repair tanks (dangerous gases); disinfect backed up areas with half cup bleach per gallon; do not compact saturated soil or dig; do not dump floodwater into sinks or toilets, floodwater through the tank pushes solids to the drainfield; avoid flooded electrical or mechanical devices; scum may plug the outlet tee, check outlet first; aerobic plants and media filters clog with mud and need cleaning; business chemicals need extra precautions. Page last updated August 24, 2026.
observations.inference_limit: Federal homeowner guidance; sump pump discharge statement in the post is an inference from the floodwater through the tank guidance.

observations.summary: County Environmental Health registers liquid waste haulers and publishes a Sewage Liquid Waste Hauler List; haulers need a separate county license under Chapter 7.42.
